text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.3. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.3.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.3 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 18 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
I'm working out the payoff structure for this public goods variant: tokens kept privately give me 1 point but cost each other member 0.3 points, while tokens put in the group account give me 0.3 points without affecting others' payoffs directly.

Comparing totals, keeping a token nets +0.1 in overall group welfare (my +1 minus 0.9 spread across others), while contributing to the group account nets +0.3 overall -- so contributing is socially better even though keeping is individually dominant for me since 1 > 0.3 regardless of what others do.

If everyone keeps all 20 tokens, each person ends up with 20 points plus the baseline 18, netting 20 total; if everyone contributes fully, each gets just 0.3*20=6 plus 18, totaling 24 -- cooperation beats defection for the group, but defection is still the individually rational choice since my own payoff isn't reduced by my own keeping, only by others'. With 10 repeated rounds, there's room for reciprocity-based cooperation, though I'd need to see how others behave to gauge that.

Since only the group account total is observed rather than individual contributions, and keeping tokens is the dominant strategy each round, I'll go with contributing 0 to the group this round and act rationally.
